tools.name: rotase_health
tools.description: Read-only check that the Rotase scheduling service is available. Use this when connectivity or service availability is uncertain. It does not require a project and does not change data.

tools.name: rotase_examples
tools.description: Read an example store, employees and complete project payload. Defaults to English labels; pass a supported language code to localize names. tools.name: rotase_create_demo_project
tools.description: Create a localized demonstration project using the same project-creation operation as the Rotase API. tools.name: rotase_validate_project
tools.description: Validate a complete Rotase project payload without saving or modifying it. Use rotase_examples first if the payload shape is unknown. Call this before feasibility checks or schedule generation. The input is the project object itself, not a wrapper with an additional "project" property.

tools.name: rotase_generate_schedule
tools.description: Generate a monthly employee schedule from a complete Rotase project payload. Use rotase_examples to obtain a template, then rotase_validate_project first. The operation calculates and returns a schedule; it does not save a project, modify browser storage or create an account. Explain returned violat

tools.name: rotase_check_feasibility
tools.description: Check whether a complete Rotase project can satisfy opening hours, staffing requirements, availability, rest rules and work-hour limits. Use after rotase_validate_project and before generation when the user asks whether a schedule is possible. This operation is read-only and does not save or modify

tools.name: rotase_schedule_report
tools.description: Calculate per-store and per-employee statistics for a generated monthly schedule. Pass the complete project object and either provide the generated schedule as the top-level "schedule" property or put it in the project schedules array. This operation is read-only and does not save data.

tools.name: rotase_export_csv
tools.description: Export a generated monthly schedule as spreadsheet-compatible CSV. Pass the complete project object and either provide the generated schedule as the top-level "schedule" property or put it in the project schedules array. The response contains the CSV text; nothing is saved on the server.
